# Two obstructions to an unrestricted-center mixture interpolation

For a probability measure mu in a finite-dimensional affine Euclidean
space, define depth_mu(y) using every closed ambient halfspace
containing y. This note refutes the proposed bound

    max_y depth_mu(y)>=1/(r-1+1/gamma_D),                  (1)

for mixtures of r uniform convex-body measures of component dimension
at most D. The second example uses two full-dimensional rectangular
fibers of an actual convex-induced mixed-integer set. Neither example
is a counterexample to OC.

## 1. Complementary simplex faces: exact depth gamma_D/r

Let r>=2,D>=1. Partition the r(D+1) vertices of an affine simplex into
r disjoint groups of D+1 vertices. Write K_i for the D-simplex spanned
by group i. Give each K_i its normalized intrinsic uniform measure
with mixture weight 1/r. Different component faces have disjoint
affine coordinate blocks. We claim

    max_(y in conv(union_i K_i)) depth_mu(y)=gamma_D/r.    (2)

For the lower bound use g=r^(-1)sum_i g_i, where g_i is the centroid
of K_i. Every closed halfspace containing g contains at least one g_i:
apply its affine defining functional and average. The ordinary
Grunbaum inequality on that simplex then contributes at least
gamma_D/r. This includes halfspaces whose boundary contains an entire
component, in which case that component contributes the larger mass
1/r. The same argument only needs the classical simplex form of
Grunbaum's inequality.

For completeness, the upper simplex bound needed below is elementary.
At a point x of a D-simplex, some barycentric coordinate lambda_j(x)
is at least 1/(D+1). The closed simplex cap lambda_j>=lambda_j(x)
has relative volume (1-lambda_j(x))^D<=gamma_D.

Every y in the full simplex has a unique join decomposition

    y=sum_i t_i x_i, t_i>=0, sum_i t_i=1, x_i in K_i

where x_i is unique whenever t_i>0. Choose any i with t_i>0. Choose
an affine function ell_i on aff(K_i) with ell_i(x_i)=0 whose positive
cap has relative volume at most gamma_D, using the preceding
barycentric construction. For epsilon>0 extend affinely to the whole
simplex by prescribing the values

    ell_i+epsilon(1-t_i)/t_i on K_i,
    -epsilon on each K_j, j!=i.

The disjoint vertex blocks make this affine extension well-defined.
Its value at y is zero, and its positive closed halfspace misses every
other K_j. On K_i the cap decreases, as epsilon decreases to zero,
to the chosen closed cap. Continuity from above of the finite uniform
measure therefore proves depth_mu(y)<=gamma_D/r. This use of an
infimum is intentional: the limiting halfspace can acquire full
boundary mass on the other components, and its mass is not substituted
for the limit of the cap masses. Points outside the convex hull have
depth zero by strict separation. This proves (2).

Since gamma_D<1 and r>1,

    gamma_D/r < gamma_D/[1+(r-1)gamma_D],

which is exactly the right side of (1). In the smallest case r=2,D=1,
take the two opposite edges [0,e_1] and [e_2,e_3] of the standard
tetrahedron, with equal uniform weights. Their unrestricted maximum
depth is 1/4, while (1) would demand 1/3. Here the continuous centroid
of the four vertices supplies the lower bound by the elementary fact
that an interval halfspace containing its midpoint has at least half
its length; no higher-dimensional Grunbaum theorem is needed.

## 2. Two parallel rectangular fibers, both full-dimensional

Let epsilon=1/10 and, in R^2, put

    K_0=[-1,1] x [-epsilon,epsilon],
    K_1=[-epsilon,epsilon] x [-1,1].

In R x R^2 use

    C=conv(({0} x K_0) union ({1} x K_1)),
    S=C intersect (Z x R^2).

C is a compact convex body with nonempty three-dimensional interior.
Its projection is [0,1], so S consists exactly of the two specified
fibers. Both are two-dimensional rectangles of area 4epsilon.
The intrinsic measure is H_2, its total mass is M=8epsilon, and its
normalized restriction is the equal mixture of these two uniform
measures. Also conv(S)=C.

We first identify an unrestricted global deepest point using only
symmetries. Depth superlevel sets are convex: if a halfspace contains
a convex combination of points, its affine functional is nonnegative
at at least one of the points. Thus the depth at a convex combination
is at least the minimum depth of the constituent points. Depth is
also invariant under an affine bijection preserving mu, because such
a bijection permutes all closed ambient halfspaces.

The two coordinate reflections x->-x and y->-y preserve mu. Averaging
their four images shows

    depth(z,0,0)>=depth(z,x,y).

The affine symmetry (z,x,y)->(1-z,y,x) also preserves mu. Averaging
its images at (z,0,0) and (1-z,0,0) now shows that

    g=(1/2,0,0)

is an unrestricted global deepest point. This argument applies to
every point of the ambient space and does not require continuity of
depth or absence of boundary mass.

The closed ambient halfspace

    H={x-2epsilon z>=-epsilon}

contains g on its boundary. In fiber zero it cuts x>=-epsilon and
therefore captures area 2epsilon(1+epsilon). In fiber one it cuts
x>=epsilon and captures only a boundary edge, whose H_2 measure is
zero. Hence

    max_y depth_S(y)=depth_S(g)
       <=(1+epsilon)/4=11/40.

The proposed interpolation (1) with r=2,D=2 would require

    1/(1+1/gamma_2)=4/13,
    4/13-11/40=17/520>0.

This is an exact counterexample to (1) using parallel positive-volume
fibers with convex compatibility. The displayed 11/40 is a proved
upper bound; no claim that it is the exact maximum is needed. The
OC threshold here is gamma_2/2=2/9, which is smaller than the bound
above. No contradiction to OC follows.
